responsibility: This module is the GCC target backend for the Altera/Intel Nios II architecture, covering both the core processor description and its bare-metal ELF, GNU/Linux, and RTEMS subtargets. Its main responsibility is to map GCC’s generic RTL, ABI, and option machinery onto Nios II-specific code generation: the central backend implementation and headers define architectural properties, register layout, calling convention, frame handling, address legitimacy, small-data and section selection, PIC/TLS and relocation behavior, builtin and custom-instruction support, asm printing, and target hooks; the main machine description and companion predicate/constraint files describe legal operands, instruction patterns, scheduling attributes, synchronization sequences, and compressed or multiword transfer forms such as CDX ldwm/stwm push/pop; and the option and subtarget files declare Nios II feature switches and apply environment-specific specs, libraries, ABI choices, and startup conventions. Together, these files distinguish this module as the architecture-specific instruction-selection, ABI, atomic, and subtarget policy layer for Nios II within GCC.
